one_liner: Senior information security manager at the Missile Defense Agency, running agency-wide classified information protection, self-inspections, and security incident inquiries under DoDM 5200.01.
fit_summary: This role requires a year of GS-11-equivalent experience in at least 3 of 5 specialized classified information security areas, such as marking, self-inspections, and incident inquiries. Nothing on file shows Daniel doing information security work at IEM, and emergency management consulting is a different field. Daniel's policy knowledge and relationship skills help only with the stakeholder coordination element.
eligibility: Open to the public, veterans, and military spouses (hiring paths: public, vet, mspouse), so you do not need federal status.
You must show one year of specialized experience at the NH-02/GS-11 level in at least 3 of the 5 listed areas, and education cannot substitute.
The position requires Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) eligibility, which means a Top Secret-level background investigation.
The posting opens 2026-10-23 and closes 2026-11-02, a short window under AcqDemo Direct Hiring Authority.
strategy: Apply only if your IEM work involved handling classified material, serving as a security manager or custodian, or doing compliance reviews. Without at least 3 of the 5 specialized areas, you will be rated not qualified.

If you did hold a clearance or work with classified or controlled information at IEM, describe it concretely using the posting's terms, such as marking, storage, transmission, destruction, and inquiries.
Frame any IEM compliance or assessment work as program reviews: planning reviews, finding vulnerabilities, reporting metrics, and driving corrective actions. Do this only where it is accurate.
Present client coordination with federal agencies and contractors as stakeholder coordination and team leadership, with dates and hours per week, on a two-page resume.
A better near-term path is entry-level security assistant or emergency management roles at GS-9 or GS-11, which would build toward this job.
resume_bullets: Led [number]-person team of [government/contractor] staff conducting [compliance reviews/assessments] for [client agency], identifying [type] vulnerabilities and tracking corrective action plans to closure.
Coordinated [program/process] across [agencies/partners], briefing [senior officials] on [topic] and resolving conflicting [policy/guidance] issues.
Served as [security role, if any] responsible for safeguarding and accountability of [classified/controlled] information per [DoDM 5200.01 or other policy].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would plan an agency-wide information security self-inspection.
Describe a security incident or violation you investigated and the corrective actions that followed.
How do you resolve a derivative marking discrepancy when source guidance conflicts?
How have you led mixed government and contractor teams across multiple organizations?
watch_outs: The specialized experience in classified information security appears to be a major gap based on what is on file.
SCI eligibility is required, which brings a lengthy background investigation.
The application window is only about 10 days.
Promotion potential is none, and the job is not remote.
